title: What are some unwritten rules you've encountered in EVE Online?

posts.cooked:
I'm a philosophy student writing about social norms encountered in virtual worlds (such as video games and social media). I would love to hear any stories about 'unwritten rules' that people have noticed while playing EVE Online (or any other games that you play).
Examples might include:
1. Things that everyone does while meeting a new player
2. Things that are generally considered rude.
3. Traditions unique to your game
4. Social expectations that new players frequently violate
If I use your example, I'll cite your username in my paper unless you would rather remain anonymous.

If your chat is lighting up with ways to turn X amount of money into lots more, don't believe them. There are better classic blunders to make, like starting a land war in Asia.

If somebody is flipping pods (stealing your loot) in a T3 Destroyer just let them. They aren't there for loot, they're there to kill you.

Combat scanning probes, just assume they've found you. Some people are exceptionally fast scanners.

Getting through null in a cheap ultra-fast align ship is generally easier if you shout "I'M JUST TRYING TO GET HOME TO MY WOMAN!" some groups will think it's funny and then cheer you on at later gatecamps.

As a personal note, I do not believe that videogames give you any practical data for real world philosophy and that this is a fool's errand.

Wow, blud seriously scraped the well's 13-year-old bottom just to pretend that someone's funny topic from the Xbox One days is serious business.

There's this certain je ne sais quoi about EVE carebears that's just...mwah, chef's kiss.

- at the end of a pvp fight, always type "gf" in local (stands for "good fight"). if you're the winner, it shows that you're gracious. if you're the loser, it shows that you're resilient.

- if you end up in a fair fight, someone made a mistake.

- if you kill a newbie outside of high sec, it's usually polite to compensate them for their loss. you want them to get back on their feet, and not to quit.

- never trust a contract that's posted in Jita local. it's always a scam.

- never leave an exploration site unfinished. complete them so they can respawn.

- if in doubt, shoot it
